body.statement: Let \(\theta_{0j}=\arctan(b_{2j}/b_{1j})\). For the full-cell conditional power \(\Pi_j\), every maximizer of \(\theta_j\mapsto\Pi_j(\rho,\theta_j,\ell_s)\) lies in \( (\theta_{0j},\pi/2]\) when \(\Delta_j>0\), equals \(\theta_{0j}\) uniquely when \(\Delta_j=0\), and lies in \( (0,\theta_{0j})\) when \(\Delta_j<0\). These are exact equality strata for every active \(j=(C,s)\in J\).
body.justification: The discrepancy index converts a two-dimensional weight search into a signed one-sided problem and identifies the proportional equality case.
body.gap: Freidling, Zhao, and Gao suggest adaptive weighting, while Chen and Andrews study leftover Gaussian information; neither derives this primitive sign rule for enrichment holdouts.
body.consumer: A trial designer obtains a falsifiable rule for whether stage 1 must receive more or less weight than the proportional-information benchmark.
body.proof_tex:
Fix an active pair and suppress its index. Put \(t=\sqrt{1-\rho}\), \(a=At\), \(\gamma=\kappa t\), \(d=b_1\cos\theta+b_2\sin\theta\), \(r=\gamma\cos\theta\), and \(v=\sqrt{1-r^2}\). For \(h=\ell_s>0\), write
\[
L=c-ah,\quad K=q_\alpha(r,c)-dh,\quad
u_0=\frac{c-rq_\alpha(r,c)}v,\quad u_h=\frac{L-rK}v,\quad
D_h=\frac{\phi(K)Q(u_h)}{Q(L)}>0.
\]
Let \(\mu(x)=\phi(x)/Q(x)\). Differentiating the bivariate Gaussian upper-tail integral and the null critical equation gives
\[
q_r=\frac{\mu(u_0)}v,\qquad P_d=hD_h,\qquad
P_r=\frac{D_h}{v}\{\mu(u_h)-\mu(u_0)\}.
\]
All divisions are valid because \(v^2\ge\rho_0\), \(Q(L)>0\), and \(D_h>0\). The normal hazard satisfies \(\mu'(x)=\mu(x)\{\mu(x)-x\}\) and \(0<\mu'(x)<1\); the upper bound is the positive-variance identity for a lower-truncated standard normal. Define the secant
\[
\bar s=\frac{\mu(u_0)-\mu(u_h)}{u_0-u_h}\quad\text{if }u_0\ne u_h,\qquad
\bar s=\mu'(u_0)\quad\text{otherwise}.
\]
Then \(0<\bar s<1\) and \(u_0-u_h=h(a-rd)/v\). With \(d'=b_2\cos\theta-b_1\sin\theta\) and \(r'=-\gamma\sin\theta\), the chain rule yields
\[
\frac{P_\theta}{hD_h}=d'+\frac{\gamma\sin\theta\,(a-rd)\bar s}{v^2}.
\]
The identity \(\cos\theta\,d=b_1+\sin\theta\,d'\) and \(\Delta=A-\kappa b_1\) give
\[
a-rd=t\Delta-\gamma\sin\theta\,d',\qquad
\frac{P_\theta}{hD_h}=\mathcal Ld'+\frac{\kappa t^2\sin\theta\,\Delta\bar s}{v^2},\qquad
\mathcal L=1-\frac{\gamma^2\sin^2\theta\,\bar s}{v^2}>0,
\]
because \(v^2-\gamma^2\sin^2\theta\,\bar s\ge1-\gamma^2\ge\rho>0\).

Now \(d'\) is positive for \(0\le\theta<\theta_0=\arctan(b_2/b_1)\), zero at \(\theta_0\), and negative afterward. If \(\Delta>0\), the last display is strictly positive throughout \([0,\theta_0]\), so no maximizer lies there. If \(\Delta<0\), it is strictly negative throughout \([\theta_0,\pi/2]\), while \(P_\theta(0)=hb_2D_h>0\), so every maximizer lies in \((0,\theta_0)\). If \(\Delta=0\), its sign is exactly the sign of \(d'\), proving that \(\theta_0\) is the unique maximizer. Compactness of the angle interval guarantees existence. The least-coordinate theorem shows that these are also the relevant individually optimized weights for the original compact alternative set.
